chunks: Muhammad ibn Ya'qub, from Abu Ali al-Ash'ari, from Muhammad ibn al-Jabbar, from Safwan ibn Yahya, from Sa'id ibn Yasar, who said:

I asked Abu al-Hasan (peace be upon him) about a slave-girl who belongs to a man, whom he circles (has intercourse with) while she is going out, and she becomes pregnant. He said: The man accuses her, or her family accuses her. I said: As for a clear/significant sign, no. He said: Then the child is attached to him.

key_terms.لَزِمَهُ: It is attached to him (paternity is established)

ai.seo_question: How is paternity determined for a child born to a slave-girl through irregular intercourse in Shia jurisprudence?
ai.summary: In this hadith from *Al-Istibsar*, Imam al-Rida (AS) clarifies the principle of *istishab* (presumption of continuity) in paternity cases involving a slave-girl (*umm walad*) and irregular intercourse (*sifah*). The ruling establishes that unless there is explicit accusation (*ittihām*) by the husband or her family pointing to another man, the child is legally attributed to the owner, highlighting the Shia juristic preference for maintaining the status quo in the absence of definitive proof.
